messages:
emma: Quick q — can we bind a fallback variant policy to a plan-level quota instead of tenant-level? trying to model free/pro/enterprise defaults for regional fallbacks.

alex_g: You mean: when primary variant out of capacity, prefer cheaper quantized variant but only for free/pro, not enterprise? :thinking_face:

emma: Exactly. enterprise gets no-fallback by default (fail-open to dedicated), pro can fall back to q4_0, free falls back all the way to distilled-sm. Need the console UX to express that.

samir: We have two axes: routing decision (region/tier/latency) and fallback policy (allowed variants + enforcement). Currently the internal API only accepts a single "fallback_chain" per tenant.

maria: That single-chain model makes it hard to express tier overrides. I proposed a small extension last week: allow policy.bindings = [{ principal: "plan:free", fallback_chain: [...] }, { principal: "plan:enterprise", fallback_chain: [...] }].

emma: Link?

maria: https://go/redwood/policy-proposals#plan-bindings (draft)

alex_g: I like bindings, but how does quota enforcement interact? e.g., free plan has a daily hard token cap. If fallback chain routes to a cheaper variant, do we still charge from the same quota bucket?

jon: We should decouple billing bucket from routing choice. Quota should be tied to tenant/plan, not variant. Otherwise tenants could game it by routing to cheaper variants and pay less.

luis: Agreed. Billing stays on tenant usage. But we can emit telemetry labelled with variant so Optimize can recommend quantization.

samir: Implementation note: our router currently picks variant at selection time and decrements capacity counters per-variant. We'd need a two-step flow: pick candidate variant, check tenant quota, then allocate capacity. Slight refactor.

emma: For console, product wants a compact view: per-plan fallback table, plus a per-tenant override toggle. UX request: show estimated cost delta if plan uses fallback chain X.

alex_g: On telemetry: add fields: routing.principal (plan/free/pro/ent), routing.variant_selected, routing.fallback_reason (capacity|latency|quota). That'll make dashboards actionable.

maria: +1. Also add trace_id correlation with rollout experiments so we can A/B fallback policies.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: policy-service v2.3 deployed to staging (2024-06-18T14:12:04Z) :rocket:

emma: Nice. Can we sketch a small example config that console might show?

samir: Sure — rough example:

```json
{
  "policy": "region-aware-routing",
  "bindings": [
    {
      "principal": "plan:free",
      "fallback_chain": ["distilled-sm", "q4_0"],
      "hard_quota_behavior": "throttle"
    },
    {
      "principal": "plan:pro",
      "fallback_chain": ["q4_0", "q8_0"],
      "hard_quota_behavior": "failover-to-hosted"
    },
    {
      "principal": "plan:enterprise",
      "fallback_chain": [],
      "hard_quota_behavior": "no-fallback"
    }
  ],
  "default_fallback": ["q8_0"]
}
```

emma: This is great. A couple of questions: 1) what does "failover-to-hosted" mean programmatically? 2) how do we express regional overrides?

samir: 1) "failover-to-hosted" = if quota exhausted, route to hosted pool rather than local variant; we already have a shim for cross-region routing. 2) regional overrides can live either at binding-level or as a route condition: `binding.region: eu-west-1 -> fallback_chain: [...]`. But that gets messy in the console.

maria: UX suggestion: console shows plan-level rows and a per-region matrix column that opens a small modal to override. Keep primary authoring at plan-level to avoid clutter.

alex_g: Also need guardrails: admins should be able to lock enterprise bindings. Add a `locked: true` flag in binding schema.

jon: Security note: any per-plan override must pass through entitlement checks. We can't let a tenant admin create a binding that routes to an unsupported on-prem variant.

luis: Telemetry plan: emit a metric `routing.fallback.applied{plan,variant,region}` and a histogram for latency delta. We'll wire that into dashboard templates.

emma: Ok next steps:
- samir: prototype API change (two-step allocation + bindings) and feature-flag it
- maria: mock console UX (matrix with modal per-region)
- luis: dashboard tiles + telemetry fields
- alex_g: add billing doc note (quota is tenant-level always) and check billing edgecases

samir: I'll push a WIP branch today, feature-flag gated.

maria: I'll post mockups in #design after lunch.

alex_g: One more operational question: metrics for rollback. If we change bindings globally, want an auto-sla monitor: if fallback rate > X% for >Y minutes, revert. Who owns the revert play?

jon: Platform on-call owns automated revert. We'll create a policy alert in Grafana and hook a runbook.

emma: Thanks all. If no objections I'll add this to the next eng-platform groom. :thumbsup:

luis: :thumbsup:

ops-bot: incident-bot: noop-check - no active incidents.
